Aerococcus urinae: Gram-positive coccus (Emerging uropathogen; often forms clusters)
Candida albicans: Fungus (Yeast; the most common cause of candiduria)
Candida glabrata: Fungus (Yeast; often shows high resistance to fluconazole)
Candida species: Fungus (Yeast; general category for non-albicans or unidentified)
Chryseobacterium indologenes: Gram-negative bacillus (Non-fermenter; rare but highly resistant)
Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus: Gram-positive coccus (Includes S. epidermidis; often a contaminant/commensal)
Enterococcus faecalis: Gram-positive coccus (Group D Streptococci; common in UTIs)
Enterococcus faecium: Gram-positive coccus (Higher risk of Vancomycin resistance - VRE)
Escherichia coli: Gram-negative bacillus (The primary cause of uncomplicated UTIs)
Klebsiella oxytoca: Gram-negative bacillus (Enterobacteriaceae; similar to K. pneumoniae)
Morganella morganii: Gram-negative bacillus (Intrinsically resistant to Nitrofurantoin and Polymyxins)
Proteus mirabilis: Gram-negative bacillus (Urease producer; associated with kidney stones)
Proteus vulgaris: Gram-negative bacillus (Indole-positive; more resistant than P. mirabilis)
Providencia stuartii: Gram-negative bacillus (Highly resistant; intrinsically resistant to Polymyxins)
Serratia marcescens: Gram-negative bacillus (Often produces a red pigment; resistant to Nitrofurantoin)
Staphylococcus saprophyticus: Gram-positive coccus (Common cause of UTIs in young women)
Stenotrophomonas maltophilia: Gram-negative bacillus (Non-fermenter; intrinsically resistant to most Carbapenems)
Streptococcus agalactiae: Gram-positive coccus (Group B Streptococcus; significant in pregnancy)
